claim:s01-formation.proposition: Clonal incomplete separation with reversible adhesion produces a PERSISTENT group life cycle (group fraction=0.
claim:s01-formation.hypothesis: Clonal incomplete separation with reversible adhesion, swept over bond strength and division/fragmentation, produces a persistent group life cycle and heritable cluster traits that a non-group null does not.

claim:s02-ecological-selection.proposition: Under size-dependent predation/settling, groups gain a FITNESS ADVANTAGE over unicells (adv=+0.
claim:s02-ecological-selection.hypothesis: Under size-dependent predation/settling, simple adhesive collectives gain a fitness advantage over unicells even with metabolic exchange controlled (H1).

claim:s03-transport-limits.proposition: Oxygen/transport BOUNDS the advantage to an optimal intermediate size: small groups (size=3.
claim:s03-transport-limits.hypothesis: Coupling oxygen/nutrient/waste PDEs to growth across colony geometries predicts size/viability changes that track diffusion length and metabolic regime (C3).

claim:s04-morphomechanics.proposition: Cell geometry/mechanics (aspect ratio, topology, packing, bonds) sets collective toughness and propagule-size distributions, consistently across mechanics backends (C4) — provisional until cross-backend runs agree.
claim:s04-morphomechanics.hypothesis: Varying aspect ratio, branch topology, packing and bond strength predicts toughness and propagule-size distributions; mechanics backends agree on the summary observables (C4).

claim:s05-differentiation.proposition: Gradient-induced specialization can improve out-of-sample group performance beyond non-regulated nulls (C5) — provisional until a no-fate/random-fate null is beaten.
claim:s05-differentiation.hypothesis: Metabolite exchange plus inducible cell fate yields specialization that improves out-of-sample group performance beyond a no-fate and random-fate null (C5).

claim:s06-evolutionary-individuality.proposition: Single-cell bottlenecks / multicellular propagules sustain heritable between-group fitness better than mixed-genotype groups with cheating (C2, C6) — provisional until multigenerational multilevel-selection runs.
claim:s06-evolutionary-individuality.hypothesis: Single-cell bottlenecks and multicellular propagules maintain heritable between-group fitness gains across generations better than mixed-genotype groups with cheating (C2, C6).

narrative.question: Under what physical, metabolic, ecological, developmental, and evolutionary conditions can independent cells become a persistent, integrated, self-reproducing multicellular evolutionary individual? The existence of adherent cells is not sufficient to establish a major transition; a defensible investigation must identify a SEQUENCE of separately measurable properties — collective formation, physiological coordination, reproducible group reproduction, heritable group-level traits, and adaptation at the collective level — which may evolve in different orders and need not all appear in every lineage.
